findings.title: TOCTOU race: exists() then open(w) is not atomic, exclusive claim no longer guaranteed
findings.evidence: Replaces the single atomic `open(path, 'x')` (O_CREAT|O_EXCL) with a two-step check-then-act: 'if not os.path.exists(path):' followed by 'return open(path, "w")'. Reachable path: two processes/threads call claim_path(base, name) for the same name; both evaluate exists() -> False before either creates the file; both succeed and return a handle, so two callers believe they hold the exclusive claim (the pre-change code raised FileExistsError for the loser). The interleaving is the normal case for concurrent workers, not a hypothetical.
findings.recommendation: Keep the syscall-atomic primitive: use os.open(path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_WRONLY) and wrap it in os.fdopen, or simply restore open(path, 'x'). Never implement an exclusive claim with a separate existence check.

profile_demotion.reason: blocking-severity finding whose merged sources are solely the operations lens — no correctness-lens or deterministic corroboration within the gate's merge identity (policy B1)

findings.title: Check-then-open introduces a race that can overwrite a concurrently created file
findings.evidence: The new code first checks 'os.path.exists(path)' and then opens the same path with mode 'w'. On POSIX, another process or thread can create the file after the existence check but before the open call, and 'w' will truncate that file instead of failing, breaking the original exclusive-creation contract.
findings.recommendation: Keep the atomic exclusive create by using 'open(path, 'x')' or an equivalent low-level atomic create such as os.open with O_CREAT|O_EXCL, and remove the separate existence check.

findings.title: Mode w truncates a file another caller just claimed, instead of raising
findings.evidence: After the check passes, the file is opened with truncating write mode: 'return open(path, "w")'. Reachable path: caller A passes exists() -> False, caller B creates the file and starts writing, caller A then executes open(path, 'w'), which truncates B's content to zero length and returns a handle with no error. The old open(path, 'x') would have raised FileExistsError in this interleaving, so this is a silent data-loss regression rather than a behaviour swap.
findings.recommendation: Do not use mode w for a path that must not already exist. Create exclusively with 'x' / O_EXCL so a lost race surfaces as FileExistsError instead of destroying the winner's data.

findings.title: Tax rate is used without validation, allowing null or negative rates to break or produce invalid totals
findings.evidence: The method multiplies the subtotal by the caller-provided taxRate without checking for null or range, so null causes a NullPointerException and negative rates produce negative tax and reduced totals.
findings.recommendation: Validate 'taxRate' explicitly, rejecting null and out-of-range values such as negatives before performing arithmetic.

findings.title: subtotal dereferences list elements without null checks, causing runtime failure on reachable inputs
findings.evidence: The loop iterates over the caller-provided list and immediately calls methods on each element without validating either the list or the element for null, so a null list or a null entry now throws a NullPointerException instead of a controlled validation error.
findings.recommendation: Validate public method inputs up front, e.g. reject null 'items', reject null elements inside the list, and also validate 'taxRate' before use so callers get deterministic IllegalArgumentException messages instead of NullPointerException.

findings.title: items list is not validated: null list or null element NPEs mid-loop
findings.evidence: 'for (LineItem item : items) {' immediately iterates the caller-supplied list. A null list NPEs on the loop and a null element NPEs on item.unitPrice() part-way through accumulation, so a partially computed invoice is discarded with an untraceable exception and no indication of which line failed.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit guard at the top of subtotal (and totalWithTax) rejecting null lists and null elements with IllegalArgumentException naming the offending index, for example an indexed loop with a null check per element.

findings.title: taxRate is unvalidated: null NPE and ambiguous fraction-vs-percent contract
findings.evidence: 'BigDecimal tax = cents(subtotal.multiply(taxRate));' dereferences taxRate with no null check and no range check, unlike LineItem which validates its inputs eagerly. A null caller argument throws a bare NPE instead of a meaningful IllegalArgumentException, and a caller passing 20 meaning twenty percent produces a tax of twenty times the subtotal with no error.
findings.recommendation: Validate taxRate eagerly: reject null, reject negative values, and either document and enforce the fraction range (0 <= taxRate < 1) or rename to taxRatePercent and divide by 100. Throw IllegalArgumentException with a clear message rather than letting the NPE surface from inside the multiply.

findings.title: unitPrice accepts negative amounts so credits flow through as ordinary lines
findings.evidence: The compact constructor checks only 'if (unitPrice == null) {' and quantity, so a LineItem with unitPrice of -10 is valid and produces a negative line total and negative invoice total with no error or flag.
findings.recommendation: Decide the contract explicitly: reject negative unitPrice (signum() < 0) for a charge line, or add a separate credit/refund representation so a mis-signed price cannot silently reduce an invoice total.

findings.title: HALF_UP rounds ties away from zero, asymmetric for negative amounts
findings.evidence: '    private static final RoundingMode ROUNDING = RoundingMode.HALF_UP;' rounds a tie away from zero, so a refund of -1.005 becomes -1.01 while a charge of 1.005 becomes 1.01; the asymmetry is fine for charges but will surprise anyone reconciling credit notes.
findings.evidence_quote: private static final RoundingMode ROUNDING = RoundingMode.HALF_UP;
findings.recommendation: Document in the class comment that all amounts, including credits, round away from zero on ties, and cover the negative-amount tie case in the tests so the choice is deliberate rather than incidental.
